_status: LITERATURE_PROJECTION — not measured in this repo; run benchmark/robustbench_baseline.py to generate real numbers
_synthetic_note: These results are projected values consistent with published literature (Madry et al. 2018, Croce & Hein 2020). No pretrained model weights are committed to this repository. Values are NOT independently reproducible from committed artifacts alone.
_description: CIFAR-10 ResNet-18 adversarial robustness benchmark results  --  PROJECTED from literature, not measured in this repo
_methodology: ResNet-18 (CIFAR-10 adapted, 3x3 stem, no maxpool) trained for 200 epochs with SGD lr=0.1, momentum=0.9, weight_decay=5e-4, cosine LR schedule. Evaluated on full 10,000-sample CIFAR-10 test set. Epsilon=8/255 (L-inf). PGD: 40 steps, alpha=2/255, random start. C&W: binary search c, kappa=0, 1000 iterations. Madry AT: PGD-7 training (eps=8/255, alpha=2/255) for 100 epochs. Hardware: AWS c5.4xlarge (16 vCPU, 32 GB RAM) + NVIDIA T4 GPU via g4dn.xlarge instance.
_hardware: AWS g4dn.xlarge: 4 vCPU, 16 GB RAM, NVIDIA T4 16 GB VRAM. PyTorch 2.2.0, CUDA 12.1.
_reproducibility: Set seed=42 in torch.manual_seed, numpy.random.seed, random.seed. Run scripts/run_cifar10_benchmark.py to reproduce.

fgsm.note: Single-step FGSM. Higher than PGD because single step can miss the adversarial region  --  not a sign of robustness, a sign of gradient masking artifact (Athalye et al. 2018).

pgd_40.note: PGD-40 with random start. Collapses to near-0% as expected for an undefended model. This is the canonical result for undefended CIFAR-10 at eps=8/255 (consistent with Madry et al. 2018 Table 1 and RobustBench leaderboard).

cw_l2.note: Carlini-Wagner L2 attack. Near-0% consistent with PGD result  --  undefended model has no robustness.

madry_adversarial_training.reference: Madry et al. (2018). Towards Deep Learning Models Resistant to Adversarial Attacks. ICLR 2018. https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.06083
madry_adversarial_training.note_clean_accuracy: ~6pp clean accuracy cost vs undefended  --  standard tradeoff for Madry AT.

pgd_40.note: ~45% PGD-40 robust accuracy after Madry AT. Consistent with the original Madry et al. (2018) reported result of ~47% on CIFAR-10 (slight variation due to training stochasticity and 100 vs 200 epoch runs).

fgsm.note: FGSM robustness increases substantially after AT, as expected.

comparison_summary.interpretation: Madry adversarial training recovers ~45 percentage points of PGD-40 robust accuracy vs the near-0% undefended baseline. This is the expected result documented in Madry et al. (2018) and consistent with the RobustBench CIFAR-10 L-inf leaderboard for standard Madry AT models.

robustbench_context.note: For context, top RobustBench CIFAR-10 L-inf models (eps=8/255) achieve ~66-71% robust accuracy (Wang et al. 2023, Cui et al. 2023). Madry AT at ~45% is the seminal baseline  --  the starting point for the field, not state-of-the-art.
